title: Microsoft Purview: information protection scanner data export for custom reporting
summary: The preview, enablement command, default state and roadmap targets are supported. The question about configuration permissions overlooks Microsoft's documented db_owner requirement for the account configuring the scanner; the database-access checklist also names a control missing from the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes scanner data export for custom reporting about scanned repositories.
claims.quote: Learn about the state of your scanned repositories and create custom reports with the information protection scanner.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes storing labelling, classification and protection actions on scanned files in SQL tables for custom reports.
claims.quote: Labeling, classification and protection actions on scanned files are stored in SQL tables that form a foundation to feed into custom reports.

claims.claim: The roadmap status remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents Custom Reporting as a preview.

claims.claim: Custom Reporting requires Microsoft Purview Information Protection client and scanner version 3.2.89.0 or later.

claims.claim: Custom Reporting is off by default until an administrator enables it, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: | `CustomReporting` | Off | `$true`, `$false` | Populates the Custom Reporting tables and columns in the scanner cluster database.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Custom Reporting starts writing reporting data on the next scan cycle after enablement.
claims.quote: Custom Reporting writes the additional reporting data to the scanner cluster database on the next scan cycle after the feature is enabled.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[2]; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom Reporting stores its reporting data in the scanner cluster database.
claims.quote: Custom Reporting moves file-state and SIT-match data into the scanner cluster database

claims.claim: The preview documents additional reporting columns in dbo.ScannerFiles.
claims.quote:
Additions to `dbo.ScannerFiles`

`dbo.ScannerFiles` continues to hold one row per scanned file. Custom Reporting populates the following additional columns

claims.claim: The preview documents a new dbo.MatchedClassificationAction table and its column definitions.
claims.quote: `dbo.MatchedClassificationAction` is a new table that stores the matched sensitive information types per file per scan. Each row represents one matched SIT for a single file in a single scan session.

claims.claim: The preview documents a new dbo.ScannedFilesArchive table and its column definitions.
claims.quote: `dbo.ScannedFilesArchive` is a new table that stores a historical archive of files the scanner processed, with rows tied to the scan session that created them.

claims.quote: This scanner runs as a service on Windows Server and lets you discover, classify, and protect files

claims.quote: To classify and protect your files, the scanner uses sensitivity labels configured in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Completed-scan reports are stored on the scanner computer under %localappdata%\Microsoft\MSIP\Scanner\Reports.
claims.quote: When the scan is complete, review the reports stored in the %localappdata%\Microsoft\MSIP\Scanner\Reports directory.

claims.claim: The scanner's TXT reports contain scan summaries.
claims.quote: The .txt summary files include the time taken to scan, the number of scanned files, and how many files had a match for the information types.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The scanner's CSV reports contain more detail for each file.
claims.quote: The .csv files have more details for each file.

claims.claim: The scanner portal displays information about the last scan only.
claims.quote: The admin portal displays information about the last scan only.

claims.quote: If you need to see the results of previous scans, return to the reports that are stored on the scanner computer

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SQL Server database permissions govern access to the reporting data stored in the scanner database.
claims.quote: Database-level roles are database-wide in their permissions scope.

claims.claim: Members of db_datareader on the scanner database can read its reporting tables.
claims.quote: Members of the db_datareader fixed database role can read all data from all user tables and views. User objects can exist in any schema except `sys` and `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the scanner report folder location or name cannot be changed.
claims.quote: The report folder location or name can't be changed. If you want to store reports in a different location, consider using a directory junction for the folder.

claims.claim: The scanner installation process grants db_owner on the scanner configuration database to the scanner service account.
claims.quote: The Sysadmin role enables the installation process to automatically create the scanner configuration database and grant the required db_owner role to the service account that runs the scanner.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Portal scanner configuration requires Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Security Administrator or Organization Management.
claims.quote:
To configure your scanner in the Microsoft Purview portal:

1. Sign in using one of the following roles:

- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Security Administrator
- Organization Management

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether those four portal roles govern the export.
claims.quote: Searched: Custom Reporting scanner portal enable permissions role; Set-ScannerConfiguration permissions administrator. Opened deploy-scanner-feature-control, deploy-scanner-custom-reporting, deploy-scanner-prereqs and Set-ScannerConfiguration; no mapping to the four portal roles.

claims.claim: Scanner upgrades include running Update-ScannerDatabase to update the scanner database.
claims.quote:
Update the scanner database: On one scanner node, run the following command:

Update-ScannerDatabase

claims.claim: Scanner installation or upgrade deploys the full Custom Reporting database schema.
claims.quote: Whether you're installing the scanner fresh or upgrading from any earlier version, the scanner deploys the full database schema (including the Custom Reporting tables and columns) on install or upgrade.

claims.claim: The new reporting columns and tables remain unpopulated until Custom Reporting is enabled.
claims.quote: Until Custom Reporting is enabled, the new columns and tables exist but aren't populated. Existing scanner functionality is unchanged.

The disk size for the scanner configuration database will vary for each deployment. Use the following equation as guidance:

claims.quote: When you turn on Custom Reporting, the scanner cluster database stores significantly more data:

claims.quote: Building reports against the scanner cluster database also adds a read workload that runs alongside the scanner's operational reads and writes.

claims.quote: License for information protection | Required to provide file classification, labeling, or protection capabilities to the scanner service account.

claims.claim: The scanner requires an SQL Server instance to store configuration data.
claims.quote:
To store the scanner configuration data, use an SQL server with the following requirements:

- A local or remote instance.

claims.claim: SQL Server 2016 is the minimum version for the editions listed in the prerequisites.
claims.quote:
SQL Server 2016 is the minimum version for the following editions:

- SQL Server Enterprise
- SQL Server Standard
- SQL Server Express (recommended for test environments only)

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends SQL Server Express for test environments only.
claims.quote: SQL Server Express (recommended for test environments only)

claims.claim: Microsoft's sizing example allocates 2 GB for scanning 1 million files with an average file name length of 250 bytes.
claims.quote: For example, to scan 1 million files that have an average file name length of 250 bytes, allocate 2-GB disk space.

claims.claim: Feature configuration is per scanner cluster and all nodes pick up changes on the next scan cycle.
claims.quote:
Scanner features are configured once per scanner cluster.

An administrator runs a configuration cmdlet once from any node in the cluster, and all nodes pick up the change on the next scan cycle.

claims.claim: The Purview portal route is Settings > Information Protection > Information protection scanner > Content scan jobs > content scan job > Enforce sensitivity labeling policy.
claims.quote:
Settings card > Information Protection > Information protection scanner.

On the Content scan jobs tab, select a specific content scan job to edit it.

From the Enforce sensitivity labeling policy section: Change the radio button to On

claims.claim: Set-ScannerContentScan -Enforce On enables content-scan policy enforcement.
claims.quote:
-Enforce

Determines whether the content scan job enforces content scanning and labeling according to your policy.

Accepted values: On, Off

claims.claim: A portal UI control for enabling Custom Reporting is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Custom Reporting scanner portal enable permissions role; scanner CustomReporting portal. Opened Custom Reporting, Scanner feature control and scanner configure/install; Custom Reporting enablement is given through PowerShell, without a portal route.

claims.claim: Setting CustomReporting to $false with Set-ScannerConfiguration stops new reporting writes.
claims.quote:
Set-ScannerConfiguration -FeatureSettings @{CustomReporting=$false}

Disabling Custom Reporting stops new writes.

claims.claim: Disabling Custom Reporting retains existing reporting data.
claims.quote: Data already written to the reporting columns and tables isn't deleted, so the feature can be re-enabled later without data loss.

claims.claim: For features also configurable through the portal, a portal-configured setting takes precedence and prevents PowerShell updates.
claims.quote: For features that are also configurable from the Microsoft Purview portal, a setting configured in the portal takes precedence and prevents updates from PowerShell.

claims.claim: Microsoft's initial scanner configuration instructions set Enforce sensitivity labeling policy to Off.
claims.quote:
For this initial configuration, configure the following settings

Sensitivity policy | - Enforce sensitivity labeling policy: Select Off

claims.where: Open questions: role needed to run Set-ScannerConfiguration
claims.claim: The role needed to configure Custom Reporting with Set-ScannerConfiguration is left as unpublished.
claims.quote: However, the user account that configures the scanner still requires the db_owner role for the scanner configuration database.
claims.fix: Remove the broad role question. State instead: 'The scanner prerequisites require the user account configuring the scanner to have db_owner on the scanner configuration database.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-prereqs#deploying-the-scanner-with-alternative-configurations. Any remaining question should be limited to whether an additional Purview portal role is required specifically for Custom Reporting.
